sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Camillus, NY?
sections.html:
Camillus is a town in Onondaga County, west of Syracuse, and the first thing to settle is whether your house sits in the town alone or inside the village of Camillus, which lies in the southwestern part of the town. Village residents answer to two sets of local rules and tax bills, and that changes who you call at closing.

You can sell through an agent, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer from a buyer like us. About four in five Camillus households own their home, which makes the town a market of single-family sellers rather than landlords.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures show about Camillus?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 25,088 residents in the town as of July 1, 2025, a 1.0% dip from the 2020 estimates base. It is a settled suburb: 92.2% of people lived in the same house a year earlier.

A median value of $209,000 and a median household income of $85,915 describe a middle-income suburb. More than one in five residents is 65 or older, so many sellers here are settling an estate or leaving a larger house.

sections.h2: How big is Camillus and how did it begin?
sections.html:
The town covers 34.36 square miles of land, and the Census Bureau counts about 738 people per square mile. Camillus was formed in 1799 from land that had belonged to the Town of Marcellus. The Fairmount area in the southeast was once part of the Onondaga Reservation territory and was annexed to Camillus in 1834.

The Erie Canal arrived in 1825 and spurred industry, and a rail line linking Syracuse to Auburn followed in 1838. The Nine Mile Creek Aqueduct and the Wilcox Octagon House are on the National Register of Historic Places. Population grew from 6,735 in 1950 to 18,328 in 1960 and 26,841 in 1970, so a large part of the housing is mid-century or newer. A buyer of an older house will ask about the roof, the furnace and the wiring.

sections.h2: Which hamlets, neighborhoods and roads are in Camillus?
sections.html:
Camillus is a mix of hamlets and subdivisions rather than one downtown. Wikipedia lists a long run of named places, and a few anchor the housing market.

  • Hamlets: Amboy, Bennetts Corners, Fairmount, Newport, Warners, Memphis and North Belle Isle
  • Neighborhoods near the village: Fox Chapel, Weatheridge, Pioneer Farms, Westview Manor and West Genesee Terrace
  • Southern edge: Scenic Hills, Parson Farms, Stanley Manor and Sherwood Knolls

NY 5 crosses the town from east to west. NY 173 meets it near Fairmount, NY 174 near the village, and NY 321 at Bennetts Corners, while NY 695 and NY 297 run near the east town line. The town also reaches ZIP codes for Camillus (13031), Elbridge, Marcellus, Memphis, Warners and parts of Syracuse, so your mailing address may not say Camillus even when the parcel is in the town. Check the deed and tax bill rather than the postal city.

sections.h2: What does everyday life in Camillus look like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Camillus works as a commuter and shopping town on the west side of Syracuse. The Census Bureau puts the average trip to work at 21.3 minutes, and total retail sales in 2022 at about $719.6 million, or $28,576 for every resident. Health care and social assistance receipts for 2022 came to about $91.3 million.

Education levels are high: 94.8% of adults 25 and older have finished high school and 44.6% hold a bachelor's degree or more. A small general aviation airstrip, Camillus Airport, sits near the northern town line, and the former Syracuse Municipal Airport lay in the northeast part of town.

For a seller the practical point is that a retail-ready house competes with finished homes on the market, while a house with dated kitchens or deferred maintenance does not. A cash buyer prices the work and takes the house as it stands, so the comparison never comes up.

sections.h2: How do I record a deed with the Onondaga County Clerk?
sections.html:
The Onondaga County Clerk records deeds for every town in the county, and its published fee schedule shows what the paperwork costs.

  • $45.50 base fee for a deed, plus $5.00 for each page and $0.50 for each additional surname or cross reference
  • $5.00 to file the TP-584 transfer tax return, plus state transfer tax of $2.00 for each $500 of price
  • $125.00 for the RP-5217 real property transfer report on an improved residential property
  • $10.00 residential deed note to grantors, required by state law since March 2020

On a $210,000 sale the state transfer tax is $840. The clerk's records go back to 1794, so title searches can trace ownership a long way. For recording questions, the deed department's number is 315-435-8250.

sections.h2: When are Onondaga County property taxes due and how does a sale affect them?
sections.html:
Onondaga County Real Property Tax Services handles taxes for properties outside the city of Syracuse, which includes Camillus. Its office is on the 15th floor of the Civic Center on Montgomery Street, and you can view bills, print receipts and pay online.

The office states two payment dates for delinquent accounts. County taxes unpaid after March 31 and school or village taxes unpaid after November 1 go to that office, which takes calls at 315-435-2426 and accepts mailed checks payable to the Chief Fiscal Officer at PO Box 1004, Syracuse, NY 13201. The county also holds a yearly online tax auction in October, with properties listed from September.

If you are behind, get a payoff figure before you accept an offer. County exemption applications for properties outside Syracuse are due March 1, so a seller who owns the house in the winter should ask the town assessor about filing.

sections.h2: What should I check at the town level before I sell?
sections.html:
Before you list, ask the Town of Camillus code enforcement staff whether any permit on your house was left open, whether a rental on the property needs registration or inspection, and which zoning district applies. An unfinished deck, a finished basement without a permit or an old shed can all surface when a buyer's attorney orders a search.

If the property is in the village of Camillus, ask the village clerk separately for any village charges. The county notes that village taxes have their own November 1 cutoff, so a closing attorney will want both bills.

faqs.q: Is Camillus a town or a village?
faqs.a: Both exist. The Town of Camillus is a town in Onondaga County west of Syracuse, and the village of Camillus is a smaller community in the southwestern part of that town. Check your tax bill to see which one taxes your house.

faqs.q: How much is the state transfer tax on a Camillus sale?
faqs.a: The Onondaga County Clerk lists it as $2.00 for each $500 of price. A $210,000 sale would carry $840, and it is reported on the TP-584 return that the clerk charges $5.00 to file.

faqs.q: Which office records my deed after I sell?
faqs.a: The Onondaga County Clerk. The base recording fee is $45.50 plus $5.00 a page, and the RP-5217 report adds $125.00 for an improved residential property.

faqs.q: Can unpaid taxes on a Camillus house lead to an auction?
faqs.a: Yes. Onondaga County runs an online real property tax auction each October, and delinquent taxes outside Syracuse are paid through the county's Real Property Tax Services office. Clearing the balance before you sell protects your proceeds.

faqs.q: Why does my Camillus house have a Syracuse or Marcellus mailing address?
faqs.a: The town spans several postal areas, including 13031 for Camillus plus Elbridge, Marcellus, Memphis, Warners and Syracuse ZIP codes. The deed and the assessment roll show the legal location.
